name: mainnet-peak
rationale: Ethereum L1, well above chain rate. 12s slots means the chain itself offers 0.083 blocks/s, and a fast path that only holds at one block every twelve seconds has proved nothing: the cases that actually threaten the budget are bursts, not cadence -- a consumer restart replaying accumulated lag delivers as fast as the broker can push, a reorg emits a run of blocks at once, and a second chain shares the topics. So this offers 4.0 blocks/s, ~48x cadence. 250 tx/block is a busy mainnet block, giving 1000 declared tps. Alerting fraction is 1.0 -- Epic D asks for peak ALERT volume, so every generated block is made to fire; the no_alert series is empty here by design. API 100 qps, weighted toward the screening path, which is the one surface where latency is contractual. The screening route is driven as a POST because that is what it is (§11 -- a screening decision is a billable, audited event, not a cacheable read); a GET-only driver would collect 405s in microseconds and report the route as the fastest thing in the system.
